source_text: ὁ θεσπέσιος Ἡσαΐας· «Ἐπ' ὄρος ὑψηλὸν ἀνάβηθι, ὁ εὐαγγελιζόμενος Σιών.» {ΠΑΛΛ.} Ἀλλ' ὧδε μὲν ὅτι ταῦτα ἔχει, παντί τῳ σαφές. Φράζε δ' ὅπως ὁ ἐπὶ τῷδε τύπος, καὶ διὰ τῶν ἱερῶν ἡμῖν ἐσκιαγραφεῖτο λόγων. {ΚΥΡ.} Καὶ μὴν, ὦ ἑταῖρε, πάρα σοι καὶ λίαν ἀμογητὶ καθορᾷν ὡς ἐν παχυτέροις ἔτι τύποις, τὸ χρῆμα γραφόμενον· ἔφη γὰρ ὧδε Θεὸς ἐν τοῖς Ἀριθμοῖς, πρὸς Μωσέα τὸν ἱερώτατον· «Λάβε τὸν Ἀαρὼν καὶ Ἐλεάζαρ τὸν υἱὸν αὐτοῦ, καὶ ἀναβίβασον αὐτοὺς εἰς Ὣρ τὸ ὄρος ἔναντι πάσης τῆς συναγωγῆς· καὶ ἔκδυσον Ἀαρὼν τὴν στολὴν αὐτοῦ, καὶ ἔνδυσον Ἐλεάζαρ τὸν υἱὸν αὐτοῦ, καὶ Ἀαρὼν προστεθεὶς, ἀποθανέτω ἐκεῖ. Καὶ ἐποίησε Μωσῆς καθὰ συνέταξε Κύριος αὐτῷ, καὶ ἀνεβίβασεν αὐτοὺς εἰς Ὢρ τὸ ὄρος ἐναντίον πάσης τῆς συναγωγῆς, καὶ ἐξέδυσε τὸν Ἀαρὼν τὰ ἱμάτια αὐτοῦ, καὶ ἐνέδυσεν αὐτὰ Ἐλεάζαρ τὸν υἱὸν αὐτοῦ, καὶ ἀπέθανεν Ἀαρὼν ἐπὶ τῆς κορυφῆς τοῦ ὄρους.» Συνίης οὖν ὅπως ἀναβιβάζεται τεθνηξόμενος μὲν καὶ καταλήξων Ἀαρὼν, ἀνθεξόμενος δὲ τῆς ἱερωσύνης ὁ ἐξ αὐτοῦ, τοῦτ' ἔστιν, ὁ Ἐλεάζαρ; Κατασημήνειε δ' ἂν τὸ ὄρος τὸ περίοπτόν τε καὶ τὸ ὑψοῦ, καὶ τὸ ἐν δόξῃ περιφανές. Λελέχθω δὴ οὖν παντί τῳ λοιπὸν πρὸς ἱερουργίαν ἠγμένῳ· «Οὐ δύναται πόλις κρυβῆναι ἐπάνω ὄρους κειμένη.»
pass_a_gloss: [cont.] …the divine Isaiah: 'on a high mountain go up, the one evangelizing Zion.' || PALL.: But that these things hold thus is clear to everyone. Tell how the type on this was also shadow sketched for us through the sacred words. || CYR.: And indeed, O companion, it is in your power very effortlessly to look down on the matter written as in still thicker/coarser types; for God said thus in Numbers to the most holy Moses: [Num 20:25–28 LXX: take Aaron and Eleazar his son and bring them up to Hor the mountain before all the congregation; and strip Aaron of his robe and clothe Eleazar his son, and Aaron, being added (= gathered), let him die there. And Moses did as the Lord commanded him, brought them up to Mount Hor before all the congregation, stripped Aaron of his garments, clothed Eleazar his son with them, and Aaron died on the top of the mountain.] Do you understand then how Aaron is brought up, about to die and come to an end, and the one from him, that is Eleazar, about to hold on to the priesthood? The mountain would signify what is seen round and on high and conspicuous in glory. Let it be said then to everyone henceforth led to priestly ministry: 'a city cannot be hidden lying on a mountain.'
pass_b_english: Cyril: …‘Go up on a high mountain, you who bring good news to Zion.’ (Isaiah 40:9)
Palladius: Anyone can see that this is so. But tell me how the type of this was also foreshadowed for us in the sacred words.

Cyril: Indeed, my friend, you can see the matter quite effortlessly, written out as it were in still coarser types. For God spoke thus to the most holy Moses in Numbers: ‘Take Aaron and Eleazar his son, and bring them up to Mount Hor before the whole congregation; and strip Aaron of his robe, and put it on Eleazar his son; and let Aaron be gathered, and die there. And Moses did as the Lord commanded him, and he brought them up to Mount Hor before the whole congregation; and he stripped Aaron of his garments and put them on Eleazar his son, and Aaron died on the top of the mountain.’ (Numbers 20:25–28) Do you understand, then, how they are brought up: Aaron to die and come to his end, and the one born of him, that is, Eleazar, to take up the priesthood? The mountain would signify what is visible from every side and set on high, what stands out in glory. So let it be said from now on to everyone who is brought to priestly service: ‘A city set on a mountain cannot be hidden.’ (Matthew 5:14)

choices.why: ἐν παχυτέροις ἔτι τύποις rendered 'in still coarser types' (more material, less refined figures).
συναγωγή rendered 'congregation' as elsewhere in Book 13.
Review: σκιαγραφέω rendered 'foreshadowed' (sketched in shadow outline);
ἀντέχομαι τῆς ἱερωσύνης rendered 'take up the priesthood'.

anf_compare.notes: No public-domain English of De adoratione Book 13 to compare. Sense taken from the PG 68 Greek. The withheld earlier English was not used as a model.

apparatus.note: Section opens mid-sentence: the subject 'the inspired Isaiah' (ὁ θεσπέσιος Ἡσαΐας) stands at the head of this section in the Greek but has been placed at the end of the English of section 21 so that sentence reads whole; only the quotation remains here. Isaiah 40:9 matches the LXX (ἐπ' ὄρος ὑψηλὸν ἀνάβηθι, ὁ εὐαγγελιζόμενος Σιων). ἐν παχυτέροις ἔτι τύποις rendered 'in still coarser types' (more material, less refined figures). Numbers 20:25–28 LXX: προστεθείς ('being added') is the LXX rendering of Hebrew 'be gathered [to his people]'; rendered 'let Aaron be gathered' without supplying 'to his people', which is absent from the Greek. The printed text has ἀνεβίβασεν αὐτούς ('brought them up') in 20:27 where the LXX has αὐτόν; followed. συναγωγή rendered 'congregation' as elsewhere in Book 13. 'How they are brought up' renders the single verb ἀναβιβάζεται, which governs both Aaron (to die) and Eleazar (to take hold of the priesthood). Matthew 5:14 matches word for word (οὐ δύναται πόλις κρυβῆναι ἐπάνω ὄρους κειμένη). Review: σκιαγραφέω rendered 'foreshadowed' (sketched in shadow outline); ἀντέχομαι τῆς ἱερωσύνης rendered 'take up the priesthood'.
